cases: WITH c AS (SELECT 1 AS id) SELECT * FROM c
WITH c(id) AS (SELECT 2) SELECT id FROM c
WITH c AS (SELECT * FROM t WHERE id < 3) SELECT * FROM c
WITH a AS (SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = 1), b AS (SELECT * FROM a) SELECT * FROM b
WITH c AS (SELECT id FROM t) SELECT * FROM c
WITH c AS (SELECT * FROM t) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c
WITH c AS (SELECT 1 AS id) SELECT * FROM c UNION SELECT 2
WITH RECURSIVE c AS (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT id + 1 FROM c) SELECT * FROM c
WITH c AS (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2) SELECT * FROM c
WITH c(a, b) AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM c
WITH c AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM t JOIN c ON t.id = c.id
WITH c AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM c
